reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: A group of glycosylation disorders affecting O-mannosylation of alpha-dystroglycan, presenting as congenital muscular dystrophy with variable brain and eye involvement
The clinical spectrum spans Walker-Warburg syndrome and muscle-eye-brain disease at the severe end to milder limb-girdle muscular dystrophy phenotypes
Severe forms combine congenital muscular dystrophy with cobblestone (type II) lissencephaly, cerebellar and brainstem malformations, and ophthalmological anomalies
Serum creatine kinase is typically markedly elevated, reflecting muscle involvement, in contrast to the usual N-linked CDGs
Standard serum transferrin isoelectric focusing is usually normal because these are O-linked defects, so a normal transferrin test does not exclude them
Muscle biopsy shows dystrophic change with reduced glycosylated alpha-dystroglycan on immunostaining; many genes are involved (e.g. POMT1, POMT2, POMGNT1, FKTN, FKRP, LARGE)
Management is supportive and multidisciplinary, addressing motor, respiratory, feeding, visual and neurological needs
reference.pathophysiology: Alpha-dystroglycan requires a specialised O-mannose-linked glycan to bind extracellular matrix proteins such as laminin and anchor the sarcolemma and basement membranes. Defects in the enzymes and glycosyltransferases that build this O-mannosyl glycan disrupt the link between the cytoskeleton and matrix, causing muscle fibre injury and impaired neuronal migration. The result is a dystroglycanopathy, with congenital muscular dystrophy and, in severe cases, malformations of cortical development and the eye. Because the defect is in O-linked rather than N-linked glycosylation, conventional transferrin screening is characteristically normal.
additionalDifferentials: Merosin-deficient and other congenital muscular dystrophies
Spinal muscular atrophy and other infantile hypotonia causes
Other causes of cobblestone lissencephaly and structural brain malformation
Metabolic myopathies with raised creatine kinase
additionalInvestigations: Muscle biopsy with immunostaining for glycosylated alpha-dystroglycan
Molecular genetic testing of the dystroglycanopathy gene panel
Brain MRI for cortical malformation, cerebellar and brainstem anomalies
Ophthalmological assessment for structural eye involvement
Respiratory and cardiac evaluation as part of muscular dystrophy surveillance
redFlags: Congenital hypotonia with contractures and respiratory compromise
Structural brain malformation with seizures or profound developmental delay
Progressive loss of motor milestones or ambulation
Severe visual impairment from ocular malformation
reference.prognosis: Prognosis ranges widely: Walker-Warburg and muscle-eye-brain phenotypes carry high early mortality and severe disability, whereas milder limb-girdle dystroglycanopathies may permit prolonged ambulation and survival into adulthood. Respiratory and cardiac complications influence long-term outcome.
pitfalls: Excluding a glycosylation disorder because transferrin testing is normal in these O-linked defects
Not measuring creatine kinase in a hypotonic infant with suspected CDG
Overlooking cardiac and respiratory surveillance in the muscular dystrophy phenotype
Assuming a single gene when the dystroglycanopathies are genetically heterogeneous
references: Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics, congenital muscular dystrophies
management: Supportive multidisciplinary neuromuscular care, as there is no disease-specific or curative therapy
Physiotherapy, orthoses and mobility aids, with orthopaedic management of contractures and scoliosis
Respiratory surveillance with airway clearance and non-invasive ventilation for respiratory muscle weakness
Cardiac surveillance with treatment of any cardiomyopathy as part of muscular dystrophy monitoring
Anticonvulsants and neurodevelopmental support where there is cortical malformation, with ophthalmological care for structural eye involvement
Nutritional and feeding support, including gastrostomy for bulbar involvement in severe phenotypes
Genetic counselling for this autosomal recessive dystroglycanopathy, with dystroglycanopathy gene-panel testing and family screening
Early palliative care discussion in severe Walker-Warburg and muscle-eye-brain phenotypes carrying high early mortality
